model: I believe employers should pay for gym memberships, or at least help cover the cost. First, healthier employees tend to take sick leave less often and have more energy, which can boost productivity. So in many cases, the membership would actually pay for itself. At my previous company, the manager introduced free gym passes, and within a few months, people in my team were noticeably less tired in the afternoons. Another reason is that it's an attractive perk. These days, companies have to compete for good workers, and benefits that support employee wellbeing and work-life balance help them attract and retain staff. A friend of mine actually chose her current job partly because of its health benefits. Of course, not everyone likes going to the gym, so a one-size-fits-all approach might waste money. Companies ought to offer a choice, for example yoga classes or a sports allowance instead. But overall, I think paying for exercise is a smart investment, and more employers should do it.
